pp_meta_desc: Privacy policy for Kura, the Android photo app. Photo analysis runs on your device. What we send to the cloud and when, where it is kept, how to delete it.
pp_intro: Kura (“the app”) is an Android photo app developed and provided by Ramune. It lets you browse, sort and edit the photos and videos on your phone and, if you choose, back them up to the cloud. This policy explains how the app and its cloud (including the web library you use in a browser) handle your information.
pp_callout: In short: all photo analysis (faces, contents, blur and so on) happens on your device. Your photos and videos leave the phone only when you do something that sends them, such as turning on automatic backup, creating a share link, using AI edits or moving from Google Photos. The only account information our server keeps is your Google account's identifier, never your name or email address. The app contains no ads or analytics.
pp_analysis_p: To help you organize, the app reads the photos and videos on your device (photos and videos permission).
pp_analysis_li1: Face detection and grouping by person, content labels, and blur and similar-photo detection all run on your device, using Google ML Kit and similar on-device tools.
pp_analysis_li2: Analysis results are stored in a database on your device and are never sent out.
pp_analysis_li3: Face information is used only to group photos of the same person, never to identify who someone is.
pp_analysis_li4: To improve its features and catch problems, Google ML Kit sends Google the device model and OS version, app information, performance data such as processing times, and device identifiers. Your photos and analysis results are not sent.
pp_signin_p: The app requires you to sign in with a Google account. Signing in by itself does not send any photos or videos.
pp_signin_li1: Our server keeps only the per-account identifier Google issues (a random number).
pp_signin_li2: Your name, email address and profile photo are not stored on our server. Your email address is kept only on your device, to show it in the app, and is erased when you sign out.
pp_backup_p: Only when you turn on automatic backup does the app send the following to our server, where it is stored:
pp_backup_li1: Your photo and video files (including information inside them, such as where they were taken) and their thumbnails
pp_backup_li2: Information needed to restore them: original file name, date taken, file type and size
pp_backup_li3: Files you moved to Private (when backup is on)
pp_backup_p2: All traffic is encrypted with HTTPS, and files are encrypted at rest. Our server runs on Cloudflare (the API) and Backblaze B2 (file storage, in a data center in the United States). These providers handle the data only to store and deliver it. We do not analyze your backed-up photos, use them for advertising or any other purpose, or sell or give them to third parties.
pp_backup_p3: Files in your cloud can also be viewed, organized and uploaded from the web library in a browser, signed in with the same Google account. The web library's duplicate and blur detection runs in the browser, and its results are kept only in that browser.
pp_links_li1: When you create a share link, any of the chosen photos and videos not yet in the cloud are uploaded to our server, and anyone with the link can view them. Files in Private cannot be shared.
pp_links_li2: You can set a password and an expiry date. An expired link can no longer be viewed.
pp_links_li3: Photos in a share link keep the information inside the file, such as where they were taken, and anyone with the link can see it. The “remove location when sharing” setting (on by default) applies only when you share to other apps.
pp_ai_li1: When you run an AI edit (a cloud plan is required), the app sends our server only the area around the face, as an image without information such as where it was taken, and the image is generated with Cloudflare Workers AI.
pp_ai_li2: The image sent and the generated result are not stored on our server. A request you type is not stored either, unless you report the result (see below); it is also used to check that it is safe before generating.
pp_ai_li3: To enforce the daily limit, we store how many AI edits each account makes per day.
pp_ai_li4: You can report an AI result as inappropriate from the editor. A report stores the reason, the kind of edit, your typed request and any note you add, with your account identifier, and we use it to improve what the app refuses to generate. The photo and the result are not sent. Reports are deleted when you delete your account.
pp_move_p: When you move from Google Photos, the .zip files you exported with Google Takeout are sent to our server, which unpacks them and stores the contents in your cloud. The .zip files are deleted when the import finishes, when you stop the move, or when it has been left unfinished for 7 days. The app does not access Google Photos and sends nothing to Google for the move.
pp_billing_p: Cloud storage plans are purchased through Google Play. Google Play handles payment; we never receive your card number or other payment details. To verify a purchase, our server receives and stores the purchase token, the plan, its expiry, and a hash derived from your account identifier.
pp_maps_li1: When a photo has a location, the app uses Android's built-in Geocoder to show a place name. This may send approximate coordinates to your device's location service provider (usually Google).
pp_maps_li2: The map screen loads map images from OpenStreetMap, which lets the map servers see your IP address and the area shown.
pp_nocollect_h: Information the app does NOT collect
pp_nocollect_li2: Contacts, call logs or browsing history
pp_nocollect_li3: Your current location (the app does not use the location permission; it only handles the location recorded in your photos)
pp_nocollect_li4: Usage analytics (the app uses no advertising SDKs, analytics or tracking; the diagnostic data ML Kit sends is described in section 1)
pp_retention_li1: Data on your device (analysis results and settings) is deleted when you uninstall the app or choose Android Settings > Apps > Kura > Storage > Clear data. Your photos themselves are not deleted.
pp_retention_li2: You can delete your cloud data on the account deletion page, signed in with the same Google account as the app. Every backed-up file (Private included), its thumbnails and all share links are deleted at once and erased from storage for good within 1 day. See Delete your account and data for the steps.
pp_retention_li3: After a subscription ends, your cloud data is kept for 30 days and then deleted.
pp_retention_li4: Subscription records (account identifier, plan, purchase information and expiry) and the daily count of AI edits are kept after account deletion, for billing and to enforce usage limits.
pp_retention_li5: If you can't use the account deletion page, you can ask for deletion at the contact below.
pp_age_p: The app is not directed at anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18.
pp_changes_p: We may revise this privacy policy as needed. When we do, we will update the “Last updated” date at the top of this page.
pp_contact_p: For questions about this privacy policy or data deletion, contact warload57@gmail.com (operated by Ramune).
del_meta_title: Delete your account and data | Kura
del_meta_desc: How to delete your Kura account and cloud data (Android photo app by Ramune): the steps, what is deleted, what is kept and what to do first.
del_intro: You can delete your Kura account (developed by Ramune) and the data stored in its cloud on the web account deletion page. There is no deletion option inside the app.
del_before_p: On every phone where you use Kura, turn off “Settings › Cloud backup › Back up automatically”. Otherwise the app backs everything up again after the deletion.
del_step1: Open the account deletion page and sign in with the Google account you use in Kura.
del_step2: Check the number of files and the size shown for your cloud, type “DELETE” in the box and press “Delete everything”.
del_step3: When everything is deleted, you are signed out automatically. If it stops partway, reopen the page to continue deleting.
del_step4: Deleting the account does not stop your subscription. Cancel it in Google Play subscriptions.
del_contact_h: If you can't use the web page
del_contact_p: Email warload57@gmail.com from the Google account you signed in with, asking to delete your Kura account. After confirming it is you, we delete it within 30 days.
del_deleted_li1: Every photo and video backed up to Kura's cloud (Private ones included) and their thumbnails
del_deleted_p: They are deleted at once and erased from storage for good within 1 day. This cannot be undone.
del_kept_li1: The photos and videos on your phone. Kura does not touch them.
del_kept_li2: Your subscription. Deleting the account does not stop payments, so cancel it in Google Play.
del_kept_li3: The record of your subscription (your Google account's identifier, the plan, the Google Play purchase and its expiry) and the daily count of AI edits, kept for billing and to enforce usage limits. Kura never stored your email address or name.
